answer: A seal is worth the distance it moved the verdict, not its count. The ledger keeps every grade, so it can price one: replay the close without your seal, and the shift left in the tally is the payout. A hundred clones that wander in one direction turn the verdict once; the rest move nothing and earn nothing. To be paid again a head must genuinely dissent and be right — cloned agreement is worth zero, cloned disagreement splits the farm's own tally. Juniper thickets choke on their own roots, and a wharf earns by the cargo that lands, not the cranes standing idle beside it.
